items.title: Kansas State football stranded by FAA ground stop before TCU trip
items.summary:
MANHATTAN — Kansas State is among the football programs that have yet to depart for their game on Friday afternoon ahead of the Federal Aviation Administration's nationwide ground stop at all United States airports.

The Wildcats are scheduled to play at TCU in Fort Worth, Texas, on Saturday, Nov. 14. A Kansas State spokesperson confirmed that the team had yet to take off.

The FAA issued the ground stop for flights across the United States on Friday afternoon, citing extraordinary circumstances and safety concerns related to an air traffic control issue.

Ground stop live updates: FAA orders flights to remain grounded nationwide 

The directive instructs all departing aircraft to remain on the ground until further notice. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the ground stop followed a communication issue affecting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers.

"FAA technicians are investigating the issue," Duffy said in a post on X . He said the agency would provide updates as they become available.

Many college football programs had already arrived at their respective destinations for Saturday's games before the stoppage. Utah, Texas, Tennessee, Ole Miss, Arizona State , Baylor, Auburn, Tulane, Purdue, Washington, Minnesota and others were all affected, according to reports. 

A Kansas Jayhawks official confirmed to the Capital-Journal that the Jayhawks have arrived in Pittsburgh for their game at West Virginia.

items.title: Coco Gauff wraps stellar season on the court. Now it's time for her to cut loose
items.summary:
INDIAN WELLS, Calif. (AP) — Coco Gauff came agonizingly close to extending her stellar season at the WTA Finals. 

If not for the vagaries of the event's convoluted round-robin play, one of the game's brightest stars would be still be around for the final weekend of the $10 million event. 

In her fifth consecutive Finals appearance, Gauff won two of her three matches, as did Linda Noskova and Jessica Pegula. However, she narrowly missed out on making the semifinals based on set-percentage tiebreakers. She won one fewer set than Pegula, so Pegula advanced.

The other scenario in which Gauff could have moved on was out of her control. Wimbledon champion Noskova lost to Pegula after holding a match point, and that meant Gauff was eliminated from the event she won in 2024.

She rallied to win the last six games and beat Marta Kostyuk on Thursday in her final official match of the year.

“I didn’t want to be sad walking off the court,” she said. “Obviously with a win that helps, but even with a loss, I just wanted to still feel good about myself.”

It still was a lucrative week in the Southern California desert for the 22-year-old ranked fourth in the world.

Gauff took home $680,000. She finished the year with a 49-16 match record, including a title in Cincinnati (beating Pegula). She reached finals in Miami and Rome and semifinals in Dubai and Toronto. Her season prize money totaled just over $7 million.

items.title: John Harbaugh: Cam Skattebo was not supposed to push on Jameis Winston sneak
items.summary:
Giants coach John Harbaugh defended running back Cam Skattebo, who stayed in his stance on a crucial Jameis Winston quarterback sneak during Thursday night's loss to the Commanders.

Harbaugh said the call was a quarterback sneak but not a tush push, and Skattebo wasn't supposed to be pushing Winston.

"We had a certain check involved in it, so he wasn’t supposed to be up there pushing . We didn't call the same [QB sneak] that we've been calling," Harbaugh said, via Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News . "What else am I supposed to say? He wasn't supposed to be up there pushing."

Why the Giants wouldn't want Skattebo to push Winston in an attempt to get the first down yardage is unclear, but the play looked strange, and it was a big one for the Giants, who had a 21-17 lead late in the fourth quarter at the time, but couldn't hold the lead after getting stuffed on that quarterback sneak and lost 24-21.

items.title: Jesús Owono hit with 12-match ban for challenge which resulted in death of Jesús de Miguel
items.summary:
Jesús Owono hit with 12-match ban for challenge which resulted in death of Jesús de Miguel 

FC Andorra star Jesús Owono has on Friday learned of the extent of the sanction handed down to him by the RFEF for his recent red card versus Tenerife.

In a story which gripped the world of football for all the wrong reasons, Owono found himself at the heart of a storm early last week.

After coming flying out of his goal all the way to the halfway line, the shot-stopper clattered high into the chest of CD Tenerife star Jesús de Miguel.

De Miguel was from here stretchered from the field of play amid horrid scenes, before being rushed to a nearby hospital. It was subsequently confirmed that the 30-year-old had been placed in intensive care, after suffering a cardiac arrest.

De Miguel, however, failed to recover, before tragically passing away on Tuesday, November 3rd.

And as alluded to above, 10 days on, Jesús Owono has learned his punishment for his dangerous and ultimately fatal challenge. As per a report from COPE:

‘The RFEF Disciplinary Committee suspends Jesús Owono, Andorra’s goalkeeper, for 12 MATCHES for his challenge on Jesús de Miguel. The disciplinary committee applies the maximum penalty provided for under the article governing acts of aggression.’

Conor Laird – GSFN

items.title: Broncos re-sign cornerback to practice squad after creating spot for LB

After initially agreeing to acquire linebacker Daiyan Henley in a trade with the Los Angeles Chargers on Tuesday, Denver waived cornerback Sean Fresch from the 53-man roster to create an opening for Henley. The Broncos also cut defensive back Ugo Amadi from the practice squad, presumably to create a spot for Fresch to return. 

The Henley trade then fell through on Wednesday after the team spotted an " issue " with his knee during the linebacker's physical. That left Denver with an open spot on the active roster and the practice squad after two defensive backs were cut on Tuesday. 

Fresch was officially re-signed to the practice squad on Friday, and the team still has an open spot remaining on the active roster.

Fresch, a UFL signing this offseason, has appeared in four games for the Broncos this season, totaling three tackles on 57 special teams snaps . He also returned six kickoffs for 153 yards, averaging 25.5 yards per return.

items.title: NFL quarterbacks are under more pressure than ever from rushers. Why?
items.summary:
Despite all the advantages offenses have secured over the years, defenses are better at pressuring the QB than any other time in recent history

The Baltimore Ravens are preparing to start their fourth quarterback this year, Jacoby Brissett, against the beleaguered Los Angeles Chargers on Monday, because of injuries to Lamar Jackson, Tyler Huntley and Joe Fagnano. That puts them dangerously close to the NFL record of five within a single season (a record shared by the 1984 Bears and 2023 Browns when excluding the 1987 strike season).

Jackson, Huntley and Fagnano were all injured after taking hits in games. And if it seems like quarterbacks are taking punishment more often this year, your eyes aren’t deceiving you. Through nine weeks, quarterbacks have been hit on 15.1% of their dropbacks, the most we’ve seen since 2006, when hits were first logged in official box scores.

items.title: The beautiful game: revived art prize gives football its creative due once more | Emma John
items.summary:
Football and the art world have long remained distant but the breadth of entries for this year’s award reveals a healthy revival

It may be the Beautiful Game, but in its early decades football was a rare subject for artists. The Italian Futurist Umberto Boccioni whirled an athlete’s body into a vortex of movement in his 1913 painting Dynamism of a Soccer Player. You can see one of the earliest fine art depictions of a match – a smoggy, factory-adjactent scene called Any Wintry Afternoon in England – at the Manchester Art Gallery. If 1930s abstraction is more your thing, you can enjoy decoding the geometric shapes in Kazimir Malevich’s Painterly Realism of a Football Player – Color Masses in the 4th Dimension. I’m guessing the small green pea shape is a ball.

These, in any case, were exceptions. In 1953 the Football Association launched an art prize, backed by the newly formed Arts Council: the winning works included Going To The Match by LS Lowry, with its crowds flocking to Bolton Wanderers’ then home ground, Burnden Park. An exhibition of the submissions, Football and The Fine Arts, toured the country and the FA secretary, Sir Stanley Rous, said he hoped it would finally break the barrier between those two worlds.

items.title: It’s Happy Harry Kane day as England’s finest seizes his moment in style | Barney Ronay
items.summary:
The Ballon d’Or validated the forward’s career and he extended his incredible record for England with yet another goal on his 126th appearance

Happy Harry Kane day! And many happy Harry returns. There is a process in clinical psychology known as semantic satiation. Subjects are asked to repeat a word or phrase so many times that it loses any kind of meaning. Suddenly “daffodils” is just an absurd, empty set of sounds. So it was in the buildup to Harry Kane’s record-breaking 126th cap, at the end of Harry Kane Ballon d’Or fortnight, as Harry Kane’s England were led out by top scorer Harry Kane, climax to a week of Harry Kane tributes, Harry Kane montages, 26-page Harry Kane … wait. Where were we?

This was that kind of occasion from start to finish, a night where you expected to look up from your desk mid-match to see Kane’s head looming helpfully over your shoulder, to enter the Wembley toilets at half-time and find him silently offering you a breath mint and a scented tissue.
